text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Lagardere chairman Jean-Luc Lagardere placed under legal investigation in connection with complaints filed by shareholders when his Matra missile unit merged with publisher Hachette in 1992.
-- French branch of Canon to restructure, cut down staff by 10 percent, expects to return to profits by 1998.
-- SNCF state-owned railway chairman Louis Gallois to present workers with plans to enhance consumer service today.

-- Longer-than-expected European Commission auditing delay and legal technicalites may jeopardize privatisation process of Thomson since offers filed by Lagardere and Alcatel-Alsthom expire on December 31.
-- Doctors' unions and social security fund to negotiate over health spending today, after government announced welfare deficit for 1997 was expected to reach 30.4 billion francs.
-- Engine manufacturer Snecma to join General Electric to manufacture engine of future large Airbus aircraft.
-- Saint-Gobain chairman Jean-Louis Beffa says his group seeks to extend market penetration in the United States and Asia.
-- 71 percent of doctors expect their income to drop in the next few years, 76 percent favour control of health spending, survey finds.
-- Daewoo Electronics considers cutting some 350 management jobs at Thomson Multimedia while creating some 5,000 new jobs, if takeover offer is confirmed.
-- Air transport association chairman says final stage of air transport deregulation to trigger growth of multinational airlines.
-- SNCF railroad turns from technology to consumer service.
